e: Amazon Pinpoint supports two-way SMS: it sends messages and receives replies, and it can stream events to Kinesis for analysis and archiving (for example, in S3 for a year). SQS and SNS FIFO don't receive SMS replies, and Amazon Connect isn't the right tool for this messaging flow.

A KMS customer managed key with automatic rotation enabled, set as the bucket's default encryption, encrypts data at rest and rotates the key every year with no manual work. SSE-S3 keys are managed by S3 and don't give you configurable annual rotation, and manual or imported-key rotation adds overhead.

The invitation-sending application can't keep up as volume grows, and SQS is already buffering requests. An Auto Scaling group that scales on queue depth adds capacity to that processing tier when the backlog grows. DAX, API Gateway, and CloudFront don't relieve the processing bottleneck.

AWS Lake Formation builds a data lake over S3 and RDS (through a Glue JDBC connection) and provides centralized fine-grained access control with little operational work. Copying data on schedules with Lambda or into Redshift adds pipelines, and RDS or S3 policies alone can't manage fine-grained data lake permissions.

A private S3 bucket accessed only through CloudFront (OAI) is the cheapest, most resilient way to host static documents: S3 is highly durable and available with no servers. Lightsail or EC2 are less resilient or more costly, and a public bucket with Transfer for SFTP adds cost and exposure.

EventBridge can match the CreateImage API call from CloudTrail events and send alerts via SNS directly, with no custom code or queries. The Lambda, Athena, and SQS options require more building and maintenance.

Putting an SQS queue in front of the DynamoDB writes, with Lambda consuming from it, buffers bursts so requests aren't lost when DynamoDB throughput is saturated, and existing users aren't affected. Throttling would reject requests, and DAX is a read cache, not a write buffer.

A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 keeps API calls and data on the AWS network, and the S3 bucket policy restricts access to the EC2 instance's IAM role (or the endpoint). Interface endpoints are a different design, and routing to S3 by IP addresses from nslookup or ip-ranges.json doesn't give private access.

ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) provides a shared, distributed session store that all instances can use as they scale in and out, which requires code changes the company accepts. Sticky sessions lose sessions when instances terminate, and Systems Manager Session Manager and STS are unrelated to application sessions.

Two SQS queues decouple collection and fulfillment so no data is lost during scaling events, and scaling each Auto Scaling group on a backlog-per-instance metric matches capacity to the queue depth, optimizing resource use. CPU-based or peak-based minimum capacity wastes resources, and SQS doesn't send notifications for scaling.

Tag Editor in AWS Resource Groups can search for resources by tag across all Regions and supported services in one query, which is the quickest way. CloudTrail, per-service CLI queries, or CloudWatch Logs Insights don't give a quick global tagged-resource inventory.

With variable and rapidly changing access patterns, Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects to the most cost-effective tier with no retrieval fees or added retrieval time (frequent, infrequent, and archive-instant tiers all return data in milliseconds), and the objects are large enough that monitoring costs are negligible. Standard-IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval charge retrieval fees.

AWS WAF is a managed service that filters application-layer attacks like XSS and SQL injection on an ALB, reducing the company's management burden. Shield Advanced focuses on DDoS, a third-party firewall on EC2 adds servers to manage, and S3 hosting doesn't protect the ALB.

A Glue crawler and a serverless Glue ETL job can convert CSV to Parquet with minimal code, and write to the destination bucket. EMR Spark, AWS Batch scripts, or custom Lambda code require more development or management.

700 TB in one month over 500 Mbps isn't possible (it would take roughly 4 months or more), so Snowball devices are required. A lifecycle policy then moves the data to Glacier Deep Archive, the lowest-cost storage for 7-year, rarely accessed backups.

Turn on default encryption for new objects, then use S3 Inventory to list unencrypted objects and an S3 Batch Operations copy job to re-encrypt existing objects in place. This is far less effort than downloading and re-uploading millions of objects, and the console can't bulk-modify them.

A pilot-light or warm-standby approach with the infrastructure in place in a second Region, Route 53 active-passive failover, and an Aurora Replica there meets the 30-minute tolerance, and the DR site doesn't need to serve the primary's load. Active-active and snapshot-based approaches are more costly or slower.

A security group must allow inbound TCP 443 from anywhere. Network ACLs are stateless, so they need an inbound rule for 443 and an outbound rule for the ephemeral port range (such as 32768–65535) for the responses. Security groups allow return traffic automatically.

A stateful in-memory application needs memory-optimized R5 instances, changed through the CloudFormation templates (infrastructure as code). EC2 doesn't provide built-in memory metrics, so the CloudWatch agent is needed for custom metrics. T3 instances are burstable, and the console or manual scaling isn't efficient.

Lambda runs on demand, scales automatically, and costs nothing when there are no requests, and it can process asynchronously within seconds. Glue jobs, EKS, and ECS on EC2 have ongoing or startup costs and don't suit idle, bursty workloads.

S3 is cheap and durable for long-term log retention, and multiple readers can access the files concurrently. EBS and instance store are attached to instances, and EFS costs much more for 7 years of logs.

Create an IAM role in the company's account that trusts the vendor's AWS account (or its role), with the required permissions, so the vendor's tool assumes the role. This avoids sharing long-term credentials. IAM users, groups with external users, and an 'AWS account' identity provider type aren't the right approach.

Give the pod permissions using an IAM role (IAM roles for service accounts), and create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB so traffic stays on the AWS network and doesn't go over the internet. IAM user keys or embedded access keys are insecure.

A Route 53 multivalue answer policy returns multiple healthy IP addresses at random, spreading traffic across all running instances. Launching four instances, two in each of two AZs, keeps balanced capacity if an AZ fails. Failover and weighted policies don't give random distribution, and an uneven 2+1 layout is less balanced.

Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed ingestion service that loads data directly into Redshift, which scales to petabytes and supports on-demand SQL analytics, with minimal operations. Streams plus S3 needs more components for SQL, Lambda on S3 doesn't provide analytics, and EC2 ingestion with RDS doesn't scale to petabytes.
